::: {.project-brief}
[What I built]{.pb-label}

- Universe-by-universe comparisons on one rolling-window protocol: 618 months; Core, Mega, Large, Small and Micro stocks.
- Sharpe ratio curves net of a proxy cost, recomputed at every one-way charge from 0 to 200 bp.
- The checklist in [Exhibit 3](#exhibit-3), which states where each check on a backtest is done in this section and the papers, and where it is still missing.

[Why it matters]{.pb-label} Before a return signal is taken to a portfolio, a researcher should ask where it works, what it costs and whether the backtest can be trusted. This page answers the first two descriptively, with the costs as a sensitivity check, and lists the checks every result in this section has passed or still lacks.

[Skills and tools]{.pb-label} [universe construction]{.chip} [transaction-cost sensitivity]{.chip} [sample splits and interval reporting]{.chip} [backtest validation]{.chip}
:::

::: {.caveat}
**Read with care.** Returns are gross of trading costs unless stated otherwise, and the brief reports no confidence intervals. Its NA-IPCA rule uses the intercept without the risk adjustment for unstable intercept estimates; [Same Forecasts, Different Portfolios](/research/same-forecasts-different-portfolios.html) reports a Sharpe ratio of 2.47 without and 2.49 with it on the same 618 months (Internet Appendix IA.G.2, p. IA-34). The characteristic library reflects today's knowledge, so every backtest here carries some hindsight (look-ahead) bias. The brief is a research communication, not a published paper or investment advice.
:::


## The setting `<span id="why-it-matters-for-practice" class="legacy-anchor"></span>`{=html}

Two questions matter before any model reaches a book: does its advantage hold across stock-size universes, and how sensitive is it to trading costs? A research brief answers both descriptively on one rolling-window protocol: 618 months, June 1973 to November 2024, with positions scaled each month to a gross exposure (long plus short) of one. IPCA (instrumented principal component analysis, a standard characteristic-based factor model) uses the plain ruler (the Euclidean or identity metric). QZ-IPCA changes only the ruler, to the characteristic ruler (the Gram metric). NA-IPCA uses the characteristic ruler and adds the intercept (the part of expected return that no factor in the model explains), with a cap on how much it may carry.

## Exhibit 1: Where across universes the models differ `<span id="exhibit-1-where-across-universes-the-models-differ" class="legacy-anchor"></span>`{=html} {#exhibit-1}

```{=html}
<figure class="blog-exhibit column-body-outset"><a style="border-bottom:0" href="/assets/img/projects/strategy-five-universes.png" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="/assets/img/projects/strategy-five-universes.png" width="1400" height="427" style="height:auto" alt="Two bar charts across five universes (Core, Mega, Large, Small, Micro). Left: Sharpe ratio difference against IPCA. NA-IPCA: +1.83, +0.64, +1.03, +1.95, +2.05. QZ-IPCA: +0.37, -0.09, +0.15, +0.06, -0.43. Right: maximum-drawdown improvement against IPCA in percentage points. NA-IPCA: +30.7, +18.2, +30.0, +16.6, +14.5. QZ-IPCA: +18.0, -9.9, +17.6, +7.0, -7.7." loading="lazy"><span class="visually-hidden"> (opens the full-size image in a new tab)</span></a><figcaption>Differences against IPCA, gross of trading costs: Sharpe ratio (left) and maximum drawdown in percentage points, higher = shallower (right). “NA-IPCA (alpha-aware)” uses the intercept without the risk adjustment. The Micro universe appears only in this brief; the later evidence report and <em>Same Forecasts, Different Portfolios</em> exclude micro caps. <span class="provenance">Source: brief <em>Adaptive Characteristic Geometry in Systematic Equity Portfolios</em>, Figure 1, p. 3.</span></figcaption></figure>
```

::: {.takeaway}
**Key takeaway.** NA-IPCA with its intercept has a higher Sharpe ratio than IPCA in all five universes, with the smallest gap among mega caps (+0.64). It changes the ruler (metric) and adds the intercept at once, so the gap is not the intercept's value alone. QZ-IPCA, which changes only the ruler, is ahead in the broad Core universe (+0.37) and behind among mega and micro caps (−0.09 and −0.43). In [Same Forecasts, Different Portfolios](/research/same-forecasts-different-portfolios.html)'s same-fit comparison, the intercept's mean-return gain is statistically significant in all four universes over 1975–2024 (every 95% interval excludes zero) but in none since October 2007 (Table IA.I.3, p. IA-46). The drawdown panel compares books of equal gross exposure, not equal volatility: in Core, NA-IPCA runs at 3.1% annualised volatility against 6.1% for IPCA (brief, Table 1, p. 2), so part of its shallower drawdown is lower risk.
:::

## Exhibit 2: Cost thresholds under a turnover proxy `<span id="exhibit-2-cost-thresholds-under-a-turnover-proxy" class="legacy-anchor"></span>`{=html} {#exhibit-2}

```{=html}
<figure class="blog-exhibit column-body-outset"><a style="border-bottom:0" href="/assets/img/projects/strategy-cost-curves.png" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="/assets/img/projects/strategy-cost-curves.png" width="1400" height="474" style="height:auto" alt="Line chart: annualised Sharpe ratio after a proxy cost against the assumed one-way trading cost from 0 to 200 basis points, Core universe. The charges at which each average return falls to zero are marked: IPCA 87 bp, QZ-IPCA 115 bp, NA-IPCA alpha-aware 137 bp, RP-PCA 146 bp. NA-IPCA starts highest, near 2.5, and falls fastest, crossing below RP-PCA at about 125 to 130 basis points." loading="lazy"><span class="visually-hidden"> (opens the full-size image in a new tab)</span></a><figcaption>Sharpe ratio of the return after a proxy cost (gross return minus the assumed one-way charge times proxy turnover), recomputed at every charge; Core universe, 618 months. Proxy turnover is each month’s raw turnover divided by that month’s book size, not trades reconstructed from holdings. RP-PCA = risk-premium principal component analysis, another factor model. <span class="provenance">Source: brief <em>Adaptive Characteristic Geometry in Systematic Equity Portfolios</em>, Figure 2, p. 3.</span></figcaption></figure>
```

::: {.takeaway}
**Key takeaway.** Under the proxy, the average return falls to zero at a one-way charge of 87 bp (basis points; 1 bp = 0.01 percentage point) for IPCA, 115 for QZ-IPCA, 137 for NA-IPCA with the intercept and 146 for RP-PCA. The intercept rule has higher turnover, so above roughly 130 bp RP-PCA has the highest Sharpe ratio after the proxy cost. These are sensitivity thresholds, not implementable break-even costs: on its 594-month sample, [Same Forecasts, Different Portfolios](/research/same-forecasts-different-portfolios.html) charges a cost on every dollar bought or sold, computed from the portfolio weights, and reports break-even costs of 68 bp for the intercept portfolio and 70 for RP-PCA; its costs are proportional only, with no price impact, financing, short-sale fees or capacity (Table IV, p. 35; p. 7).
:::

## Exhibit 3: Checks before a backtest number is quoted {#exhibit-3}

::: {.table-scroll .design-table .dt-wide}
| Check | How it is done | Where | Still missing |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Scale every book to the same gross exposure | Every model at the same gross exposure (long plus short): IPCA's maximum drawdown is −34.6% per unit of gross exposure rather than −96.0% raw (unscaled) | [From forecast to portfolio](/projects/forecast-to-portfolio.html#exhibit-2), Exhibit 2 | — |
| Compare at equal volatility | Each series divided by its own standard deviation | [From forecast to portfolio](/projects/forecast-to-portfolio.html#exhibit-3), Exhibit 3 | Scaled by full-sample volatility, known only afterwards; no ex-ante volatility target, and drawdowns here are at equal gross exposure |
| Split the sample | Sharpe ratios from October 2007 (206 months) reported separately: 1.12 against 2.49 over the full sample | [From forecast to portfolio](/projects/forecast-to-portfolio.html#exhibit-3), Exhibit 3 | Not a holdout sample: the split is retrospective, and a change across periods needs a direct between-period test, which [Same Forecasts, Different Portfolios](/research/same-forecasts-different-portfolios.html) does not run; it reports its periods descriptively (Section VI.C, p. 39; Internet Appendix IA.I) |
| Use one setting for every model | Reference factor penalty and position penalty of 0.01 for every model, ruler (metric) and date, none tuned to a model or a date; the intercept cap (0.035) never binds | [Same Forecasts, Different Portfolios](/research/same-forecasts-different-portfolios.html), p. 17 and footnote 3, p. 10 | The main-text sample and portfolio rule were chosen after both candidates had been computed, and the intervals do not adjust for that ([Same Forecasts, Different Portfolios](/research/same-forecasts-different-portfolios.html), footnote 2, p. 6) |
| Declare the specification search | State which choices were fixed before results were seen | [Same Forecasts, Different Portfolios](/research/same-forecasts-different-portfolios.html), footnote 2, p. 6: the 594-month sample and the main-text rule were selected after examining both samples and both rules, and the pointwise intervals do not adjust for these choices; [The Ruler Matters](/research/the-ruler-matters.html), Internet Appendix IA.8, p. 105: its follow-up diagnostics came after the initial model comparisons and are not presented as results from an untouched validation period | A design fixed in advance and tested on later data or another market |
| Price trading costs | Zero-return thresholds under a turnover proxy, 87–146 bp (a sensitivity check, not a break-even cost); in *Same Forecasts, Different Portfolios*, Sharpe ratios net of 10, 25 and 50 bp per dollar bought or sold, computed from the weights, and break-even costs of 23–70 bp | This page, [Exhibit 2](#exhibit-2); [Same Forecasts, Different Portfolios](/research/same-forecasts-different-portfolios.html), Table IV, p. 35 | Borrow fees, market impact and capacity |
| Report intervals, not only point estimates | Paired mean-return gain from the intercept, Core stocks: 0.49 percentage points a month, 95% block-bootstrap interval [0.35, 0.63], over June 1975–November 2024 (594 months); 0.20, [−0.07, 0.41], p = 0.11, since October 2007 (206 months) | [Same Forecasts, Different Portfolios](/research/same-forecasts-different-portfolios.html), Table IA.I.3, p. IA-46 | The brief behind Exhibits 1–2 reports none |
| State the hindsight (look-ahead) bias | The characteristic library reflects today's knowledge; point-in-time availability not verified | "Read with care" boxes | A point-in-time library |
| Adjust for known factors | Regress each book's returns on standard factors (Fama–French five plus momentum) and report the intercept (alpha) with its confidence interval | Not yet done in this section | The regression itself |
:::

IA-46); *The Ruler Matters*, Internet Appendix IA.8, p. 105.</span>

::: {.takeaway}
**Key takeaway.** A backtest number goes on these pages only with its gross exposure, volatility basis, sample split and cost treatment stated; the last column lists what is not yet measured, including a test fixed in advance and a factor regression.
